title: Machines
noBackend: This version of LordOS can't run machines.
emptyHint: A machine runs another system in a window, in its own sandbox. Start from a disk image or an ISO.
deleteDetail: The machine and its disks go to the Trash. You can restore them from there until you empty it.
deleteFailed: “{name}” couldn't be moved to the Trash.
ejectFailed: The ISO couldn't be taken out of “{name}”: is it still running?
bad.newer: Made by a newer version of LordOS
why.qemu-failed: The machine's engine stopped with an error.
why.qemu-3d-crash: The machine's engine crashed when the system inside reset its 3D graphics (a known QEMU bug).
why.guest-panic: The system inside it stopped with an error.
why.supervisor-lost: Its supervisor ended unexpectedly; it will be cleaned up at the next start.
why.forced: It didn't shut down in time and was turned off.
fix.qemu-signal: Start it again; if it keeps happening, the log below says where.
fix.qemu-3d-crash: It happens when the system inside resets its 3D graphics, which Linux does when it shuts down or restarts. The disk is checked at the next start. Switch this machine to 2D graphics until QEMU is fixed.
fix.out-of-memory: Give it less memory, or close other machines, and start it again.
fix.start-failed: The log below says what is missing.
fix.guest-panic: Start it again; if it keeps happening, the system inside needs repair.
fix.forced: Unsaved work in the machine may be lost.
win.gone: This machine isn't in the Machines folder any more.
win.noMemory: Not enough memory beside the machines already running: this one needs {need} MB with QEMU's own share, and {free} MB are left for machines. Shut one down, or give this one less memory.
win.cantAttach: The machine is running, but this window couldn't connect to it.
win.startingHint: The picture appears as soon as the machine shows one.
win.shuttingDownHint: The system inside is asked to shut down. If it doesn't answer, it is turned off after a minute.
win.noDisplayHint: This machine runs without a display.
req.title: Machines needs a few system parts
req.offline: The package sources didn't answer: check this computer's network, then try again.
req.kvm: This computer has it, but your account can't use it yet. Without it, machines are much slower.
req.noKvm: This computer offers no hardware virtualization: machines are emulated, much slower.
req.notAdmin: An administrator of this computer has to do this.
new.title: New Machine
new.name: Name
new.memoryMax: Up to {max} MB on this computer
new.importHint: The image is copied into the machine; the original stays as it is.
new.isoHint: The ISO is attached read-only and the machine starts from it.
new.rootPassword: Root password for the first start (optional)
new.rootPasswordHint: Some images ask for it the first time they start (Debian's cloud images do). Only its hash is kept, until the machine's first clean shutdown.
new.err.nameBad: Use a shorter name, without control characters.
new.err.nameTaken: There is already a machine with that name.
new.warn.vcpus: More than {n} leaves this computer little to work with while the machine runs.
new.warn.emulated: Another architecture is emulated: expect it to be many times slower.
new.warn.noKvm: Without hardware virtualization this machine is emulated, much slower.
unreadable.newerHint: {name} was changed by a newer version of LordOS. Update LordOS to start it.
unreadable.invalidHint: {name}'s description (machine.json) is damaged or incomplete, so it can't start.
first.hint: Run another system in a window of this desktop, at full speed.
first.stepText: Machines needs permission to use this computer's virtualization. It asks once for an administrator.
first.offText: This computer doesn't offer hardware virtualization. If it has it, restart, open the firmware setup and turn it on (often under CPU or Advanced).
first.emulated: You can still run a machine now, emulated. It will be much slower.
req.use.kvm: KVM, so machines run at full speed
req.use.display: The picture of a machine in its window
req.use.network: passt: the machine's own network, no root
req.fromStore: Installed from Debian's packages through LordOS.
pi.title: {board}, {ram}
pi.native: Native machines are arm64, with up to {cpus} cores and {mem}.
pi.note.amd64: Small systems only, many times slower
pi.note.nested: This processor can't do nested virtualization
pi.emuText: {name} is amd64, so this computer imitates that processor. It runs many times slower than a native machine: fine for a small server, not for a full desktop.
pi.sdTitle: Machines are on a microSD card
pi.sdText: Machines will be slow here. An NVMe or USB 3 SSD works much better.
as.step.name: Name
as.title.choose: What do you want to run?
as.title.profile: How will you use this machine?
as.title.name: Name it
as.emulated: This is {arch}, and this computer is {host}: the machine will be emulated, much slower.
as.emulatedShort: Emulated: much slower than a machine of this computer's architecture.
as.profileHint.light: A small system that leaves this computer room to work.
as.profileHint.development: More cores and memory for builds and tools; take snapshots as you go.
as.r.diskCopy: A copy of the image, at least {n} GB
as.thenStart: It starts in its own window when it's ready.
cfg.title: {name}: Configure
cfg.needsOff: Changing this needs the machine off.
cfg.runningBanner: The machine is running: settings that need it off are dimmed.
cfg.rn.folderWillBe: Its folder and its transfer folder will be called “{folder}”.
cfg.rn.running: The name changes now. Its folder keeps its name while the machine runs; once it's off, Rename Folder (below) names it “{folder}”.
cfg.rn.runningSame: The name changes now; its folder keeps its name.
cfg.rn.badName: A name is 1 to 64 bytes of text and doesn't start with a dot.
cfg.rn.folderTaken: The Machines folder already has “{folder}.lordvm”: pick another name.
cfg.rn.transferTaken: Machines/Transfer already has a folder called “{folder}”: pick another name.
cfg.rn.kept: The name is saved, but its folder keeps its old name: {why}
cfg.rn.later: Saved. Once the machine is off, Rename Folder in General names its folder “{folder}”.
cfg.rn.offer: Its name asks for the folder “{folder}”: Rename Folder renames it and its transfer folder.
cfg.onCloseNote: Suspend saves its memory to disk and the next start continues there. Shut down asks the system inside to shut down, and turns it off after a minute. Keep running leaves it on without a window.
cfg.cpuNote: With QEMU's own share the machine may use up to {limit}. At most {max} for one machine: one core and the desktop's memory stay for this computer.
cfg.graphics2dNote: 2D works with every system: the guest draws its picture with the processor.
cfg.graphics3dNote: 3D lets the guest's apps draw with this computer's GPU (OpenGL). A machine with 3D can't be suspended or keep snapshots with its memory: it shuts down instead.
cfg.pointerDrawNote: LordOS draws the machine's pointer where your mouse is, without waiting for the machine. It needs the LordOS tools in the machine, and the machine's screen blinks once when this changes. Choose The machine if its pointer looks wrong.
cfg.no3d.windows: This system has no stable 3D driver for a virtual GPU, so it stays 2D.
cfg.no3d.arch: 3D needs an amd64 computer and an amd64 machine for now.
cfg.no3d.gpu: 3D needs the desktop to draw with the GPU, and it draws without one now.
cfg.no3d.modules: 3D needs QEMU's OpenGL modules: install what Machines needs from its requirements.
cfg.no3d.node: 3D needs access to this computer's GPU, which this account doesn't have.
cfg.netNote.shared: The machine reaches the internet and the network through this computer, with its own address; nothing on this computer listens for it.
cfg.netNote.isolated: The machine has no network at all.
cfg.keyboardValue: This computer's, while the window is in front
cfg.pointerNote: Over the picture the pointer is the guest's own when the system shows one.
cfg.diskNote: Uses {used} on this computer now. A disk can grow, never shrink; the system inside may need its partition grown too.
cfg.cdRunning: Changing the disc needs the machine off in this version.
cfg.bootNote: An empty disk can't start, so a new machine starts from its ISO until a system is installed.
cfg.bootCustomNote: The machine tries them from the top and starts from the first one that has a system.
cfg.bootNetNone: An isolated machine has no network card, so this one is skipped.
cfg.bootMenu: Show the boot menu at start
cfg.bootMenuNote: Each start waits 5 seconds: press Esc in the machine's window to choose where it starts from, that time only.
cfg.secNote.sandbox: QEMU runs with Landlock, two seccomp filters, no new privileges and no capabilities.
cfg.secNote.files: It may write only its disks, and read its firmware and ISO.
cfg.secNote.network: No sockets of its own: its network goes through passt, which listens on nothing.
cfg.secNote.limits: Its own cgroup: at most {limit} of memory and its vCPUs' worth of CPU.
cfg.secNote.display: A separate sandboxed helper copies the picture; lord-server never sees QEMU's memory.
cfg.secNote.secrets: A root password given at creation is kept only as a hash, until the first clean shutdown.
fs.hint: The bar hides by itself. Move to the top edge to see it.
tb.captureOn: Mouse captured: ❖Esc or Ctrl+Alt releases it
tb.captureApps: Not in apps mode: the machine's windows share this computer's pointer
cfg.captureFsNote: In full screen the mouse moves only the machine's pointer, as games need. ❖Esc or Ctrl+Alt gives it back; a click in the picture captures it again.
cfg.pinNote: Automatic gives each of the machine's cores a core of this computer of its own, away from the ones the desktop keeps, so neither slows the other down. Nothing is pinned when there aren't enough free cores.
fail.diskSafe: The system never ran; its disk is safe.
logs.title: {name} logs
req.stalled: The network isn't answering, so nothing was installed. Check the connection and try again.
tb.cdRefused: The drive can't take a disc now.
win.netLost: This machine's network stopped and couldn't be brought back. It comes back when the machine starts again; the machine log says why.
win.netBack: The network is back ({s} s without it).
why.resume-failed: Its saved session couldn't be loaded.
fix.resume-failed: The saved session is kept. Try again, try anyway if this computer or its engine changed, or discard it and start from the disk.
close.title: Close {name}?
close.text: Suspend keeps everything as it is, on disk, until you open it again. Keep Running leaves it on without a window; its card says so.
close.no3dSuspend: With 3D graphics it can't be suspended.
close.always: Always do this for this machine
win.recovered: An operation that was interrupted the last time was finished or undone when this machine started. The machine log says which.
win.identityDone: This copy has its own identity now: a new name and machine-id inside it.
win.identityName: This copy takes its own computer name at its next restart.
discard.title: Discard {name}’s saved session?
discard.detail: What was open in it is lost, as after a power cut. The next start boots from its disk.
cfg.keepAwake: Keep this computer awake while it runs
cfg.keepAwakeNote: This computer doesn't go to sleep by itself while the machine runs. The display may still turn off.
cfg.savedNote: The next start continues where it was. Settings that change the hardware wait until it's discarded or the machine shuts down.
snap.title: {name} snapshots
snap.none: No snapshots yet. A snapshot keeps this moment so you can go back to it.
snap.aboutMemory: Includes memory, so it resumes where it was. Going back loses what changed since.
snap.aboutDisk: Taken with the machine off: going back starts it as after a power cut. What changed since is lost.
snap.offOnly: A snapshot taken with the machine off needs the machine off to go back to it.
snap.many: {n} or more snapshots slow the disk down: delete the ones you don't need.
snap.notBackup: A snapshot lives on the same disk. It isn't a backup.
snap.takeRunning: The machine pauses for a moment while its memory is saved with the snapshot.
snap.takeOff: The machine is off: the snapshot keeps its disks.
snap.goBackMemory: The machine continues from that moment, with what was open then. What changed since is lost.
snap.goBackDisk: The disks go back to that moment; the machine starts as after a power cut. What changed since is lost.
snap.takeFirst: Take a snapshot of now first
snap.deleteText: The machine can't go back to it any more. The machine keeps running as it is.
snap.startingFrom: The machine starts from the snapshot in its window.
snap.done.revert: The machine went back to the snapshot.
win.suspendedHint: Its memory is saved. Resuming continues where it was.
clone.title: Copy {name}
clone.cloneText: A new machine that runs beside this one. It gets its own network address and identity.
clone.duplicateText: An exact copy with the same identity. It keeps the snapshots and a saved session, and shouldn't run beside the original.
clone.keepIdentityNote: Inside, the copy keeps the original's name and machine-id. It still gets its own hardware ID and network address.
clone.hostnameBad: Use lowercase letters, digits and dashes (not first or last), at most 63.
clone.winNameBad: Use letters, digits and dashes, at most 15, and not only digits.
clone.identityAgent: At its first start, the guest agent gives the copy this name, a new machine-id and new SSH keys.
clone.identityNoAgent: This machine has no guest agent: the copy gets its own hardware ID and network address, but inside it keeps the original's machine-id, and its name changes only on systems that take it from the start-up settings. Turn the guest agent on in Configure to change both.
win.cloneIdentity: LordOS's tools give the copy this computer name; Windows uses it from its next restart. The machine's SID doesn't change.
clone.fullCopy: A full copy of the disk
clone.running: {name} is running: shut it down first. A machine is copied while it's off.
clone.suspended: {name} has a saved session, which holds its identity: resume it and shut it down first, or make a Duplicate.
clone.how.reflink: This disk is on {fs}, which can share files: the copy shares {name}'s disk until either of them changes. It takes a moment.
clone.how.linked: This disk is on {fs}, which can't share files. {name}'s disk becomes a frozen base, and both machines write their changes beside it. It takes a moment.
clone.how.copy: A full copy of the disk, without its snapshots: it takes a while and as much space as the disk uses.
clone.how.duplicate: A full copy, snapshots and saved session included: it takes a while and as much space as the machine uses.
clone.done: The new machine is in the library.
storage.title: Storage
storage.aboutLinked: Shares a {size} frozen disk with {n} machines; only its own changes are its. Deleting it frees {frees}. The shared disk is freed once all of them are gone.
storage.aboutShared: Shares {size} with another copy until either changes. Deleting it frees {frees}.
storage.trashDetail: It frees {size} once the Trash is emptied.
storage.whenOff: Shut the machine down to reclaim space or move it to the Trash.
storage.baseUsed: The disk {names} were cloned on. It goes once no machine uses it (in the Trash: {trash}).
storage.baseUnused: No machine uses this shared disk any more, here or in the Trash.
storage.pick: Choose a machine to see what it takes and what deleting it would free.
storage.estimate: About {frees} of its {now} can be given back by rewriting the disk without what it no longer uses. The machine stays off while it runs.
storage.cant: This disk can't be rewritten now: {why}.
storage.dlPartial: A stopped download: {size} so far. Creating the machine again continues it.
storage.dlUnused: No machine of yours has it in its CD drive.
storage.dlShared: Downloaded systems are shared by every account on this computer; removing one needs an administrator.
storage.dlRunning: Running with it in the CD drive: {names}. Shut it down first.
storage.dlRemovePartial: The {size} downloaded so far are deleted.
storage.dlRemoveUsed: It frees {size}. {names} will start with an empty CD drive.
storage.dlRemoveOthers: Machines of other accounts that use it lose it too. It can be downloaded again.
as.profileFits: A profile only sets values you can change later. These fit this computer: {cpus} cores, {mem}.
as.profileHint.productivity: Everyday work beside your apps: the clipboard both ways and the transfer folder.
as.profileHint.testing: Isolated network, nothing shared, the guest agent off.
as.profileHint.design: Accurate full screen, tablet input and 3D graphics on this computer's GPU for Linux systems.
cfg.profileNote: Choosing one sets the cores, memory and network below, for this computer; nothing else changes.
shell.title: Serial console of {name}, inside the machine
logs.overviewHint: What the machine log says, in one place
diag.opWaiting: {op}, finished or undone at the next start
diag.clean: Nothing went wrong in the last run.
agent.extraOn: Turn the Extra Display Back On
agent.extraHint: This machine has a second display that LordOS doesn't show: windows, clicks and the keyboard's focus can end up there, out of sight.
agent.offHint: Turn it on in Configure → Guest agent, then start the machine again.
agent.installHint: Install it in the machine with its package manager, for example: apt install qemu-guest-agent. It connects by itself.
agent.bootHint: The machine is starting; the agent connects once its system is up.
agent.cap.shutdown: A clean shutdown when the power button isn't heard
agent.cap.time: The clock, set after a pause or a resume
agent.cap.clipboard: Clipboard (text, rich text, pictures), the ways Configure allows
agent.toolsUpdate: A newer version of the LordOS tools is available.
agent.toolsOldTitle: The LordOS tools in {machine} are out of date
agent.toolsInstalled: The LordOS tools are installed and running in the machine; they start again at every sign-in.
agent.installed: The clipboard helper is installed. It starts again in the machine's open desktop session, and at every sign-in.
agent.clipOff: The clipboard is off in this machine. Turn it on in Configure → Sharing, with the machine off.
agent.clipNoTool: The machine has no clipboard tool. Install the helper again (it installs xclip too), or run this in the machine: sudo apt install xclip
agent.err.missing: This computer doesn't have the tools for this machine's system: update LordOS.
agent.err.busy: The machine's agent is busy: try again in a moment.
agent.err.noExec: The machine's guest agent doesn't allow copying files or running programs.
agent.err.timeout: Installing took too long inside the machine.
agent.err.noFolder: The machine couldn't prepare a private folder for the install.
agent.err.gone: The machine's agent stopped answering during the install.
cfg.clipboardNote: Text, rich text and pictures, through the guest agent's own channel, with no network, and only while you use the machine: a program in it gets your clipboard when it pastes, never in the background. Off until you choose a direction.
cfg.clipTrustNote: Trusted: a paste in the machine gets your clipboard while you use it, as on this computer. Ask: each paste into the machine and each copy out of it waits for your OK, with a preview.
cfg.agentNote: Two private channels into the machine: one for qemu-guest-agent (its state, a clean shutdown, the clock, the journal) and one for the clipboard helper. Nothing goes through the network.
cfg.agentInstallNote: Install qemu-guest-agent with the machine's package manager. The clipboard helper is installed from the Agent button on the machine's bar once qemu-guest-agent answers.
win.perfProfileNote: While the machine runs, the LordOS tools in Windows switch it to the High performance power plan and turn off animations, shadows and transparency. Everything goes back when this is off or the tools stop. Needs the LordOS tools w11 or later.
cfg.toolsAuto: Update the LordOS tools in this machine automatically
cfg.toolsAutoNote: When this LordOS brings newer tools, they're installed while the machine runs and nothing is being copied. Off: a notification offers the update.
as.shareClip: Share the clipboard with this machine
as.shareClipHint: Text, both ways, through the guest agent. Off unless you turn it on; change it later in Configure.
mig.pick: Choose the machine: its settings file (.vmx, .vbox, config.pvs, .ovf), an .ova, or a disk image
mig.refused: The import couldn’t start: check the name.
mig.title: Import {name}
mig.subDisk: A disk image, with a new machine around it.
mig.originalStays: The original stays as it is.
mig.readingNote: Its settings and disks are checked; nothing is changed.
mig.r.name: Name
mig.netSame: Shared, the same MAC addresses; you can change it
mig.netNew: Shared; cards without an address get a new one
mig.idKept: Kept: the system UUID the guest reads
mig.idNew: A new one (the source doesn’t keep one)
mig.devicesCompat: SATA disks, a {nic} network card: it starts without new drivers
mig.note.snapshots-flattened: {n} snapshots: the current state is kept, flattened
mig.note.tpm: The virtual TPM: its keys can’t be carried over
mig.note.secure-boot-off: Secure Boot: off on this machine
mig.note.boot-entries: UEFI boot entries are made again; the system’s own loader starts it
mig.note.cdrom: Disc images it had attached stay out
mig.note.shared-folders: Shared folders: set them up again later
mig.note.new-mac: A card without a MAC address in the settings gets a new one
mig.note.new-uuid: The source keeps no system UUID: a new one is made
mig.note.serial-dropped: A disk serial longer than 20 characters can’t be given to a SATA disk
mig.note.vcpus-cut: More vCPUs than this computer has: fewer here
mig.note.memory-cut: More memory than this computer can give: less here
mig.note.devices: Drivers: it starts on ordinary devices; Configure offers the faster ones once the guest has their drivers
mig.tpmWarn: This machine had a virtual TPM, and its keys can’t be carried over. If the guest encrypts its disk with the TPM, have the disk’s recovery key at hand before you import it.
mig.emulated: This machine is {arch}. On this computer ({host}) it runs emulated, much slower.
mig.license: The machine’s identifiers are copied, but its hardware is new to it: its system may ask to activate its license again.
mig.block.saved-state: The machine is suspended in the other app. Start it there and shut it down, then import it: a saved session can’t move between apps.
mig.block.encrypted: The machine or one of its disks is encrypted. Remove the encryption in the other app first.
mig.block.in-use: The other app has this machine open. Quit it first.
mig.block.too-many-disks: The machine has more than five disks.
mig.block.no-disk: The machine has no disk to import.
mig.doneNote: It keeps its MAC addresses and system UUID. When the guest has the virtio drivers, switch it to the fast devices in Configure, Disks.
cfg.importedNote: Another virtualization app’s machine, brought over with its identity. The original wasn’t changed.
cfg.devCompatNote: Devices every system has drivers for, as the other app gave it. The fast ones need the guest’s virtio drivers: install them first (a guest without them gets them from the virtio drivers’ disc), then switch. The guest then sees new disk and network controllers; the MAC address stays.
cfg.devFastNote: virtio disks and network card: the fastest. A guest without virtio drivers won’t find its disk: switch back if it doesn’t start.
mig.note.snapshot-flattened: A snapshot: the current state is kept, flattened
dl.reading: Reading the list of images on {name}'s site…
dl.found: {file}, from its maker's signed list (signature and SHA-256 checked)
dl.pinned: {file}, its SHA-256 pinned in LordOS's signed catalog (checked after the download)
dl.notice.archived: {maker} has paused its public images: this is its last one, from {date}, and it gets no more security updates. It comes without Google's apps.
dl.noList: The list of images couldn't be read: {why}
dl.noImage: its list has no image of this release for this architecture right now
dl.checked: {size}, kept only if its SHA-256 is the listed one
dl.checkedNoSize: Kept only if its SHA-256 is the listed one
dl.cancelled: What came down is kept. Continue Download picks it up where it stopped; Storage can remove it.
un.title: Install without questions
un.hint: Skips the installer's questions and makes your account; the machine then restarts into the installed system.
un.err.user: Lowercase letters, digits, - and _, starting with a letter
un.err.userReserved: That name belongs to the system
un.how.preseed: The answers go into the installer's own start files, your password only as a hash, and they are removed once the system is installed.
un.how.autoinstall: The answers go on a small disk the installer reads, your password only as a hash, and the disk is removed once the system is installed.
un.how.kickstart: The answers go on a small disk the installer reads, your password only as a hash, and the disk is removed once the system is installed.
un.image: Installs from {file}, also checked against its maker's signed list
dl.noHelper: Downloading a system needs LordOS's system helper, which isn't running.
clip.blockedRead: {name} tried to read your clipboard in the background: blocked
clip.blockedWrite: {name} tried to change your clipboard in the background: ignored
clip.blockedBody: The clipboard goes into and out of a machine only while you use it. Its log has the details.
win.stopped3dHint: The system inside shut down or restarted, and with 3D graphics the machine's engine stops at that moment (a known QEMU bug). If it was restarting, click to start it again. With the guest agent on and the clipboard helper installed, a restart starts again by itself.
first.addHint: Add a virtual machine to run another system in a window of this desktop: download one, install it from an ISO, or bring one from another app.
lib.sort.name: By Name
lib.newHint: Download a system, install from an ISO, or migrate from another app
lib.importHint: A qcow2 or raw disk image
agent.idle: Machine agent: starts with the machine
tb.sharesNone: No folder is shared with this machine
cfg.sharesNote: Up to 4 folders of this computer that the machine mounts. Read-only unless you turn on writing. Each one is served by its own sandboxed helper that sees only that folder; hidden folders, all of the home folder and the machines’ library can’t be shared.
req.use.folders: virtiofsd: a folder of this computer inside a machine
req.use.tpm: swtpm: a TPM 2.0 chip of its own for each machine that asks for one
win.ownHint: Every edition, with your own license
win.ownSteps: Download Windows 11 from Microsoft's own page: under “Download Windows 11 Disk Image (ISO)” choose {arch} and your language. Machines finds the file in your Downloads folder, checks it against the SHA-256 Microsoft publishes for it, and uses it.
win.waiting: Waiting for the ISO in your Downloads folder…
win.notMicrosoft: {file} isn't an ISO Microsoft publishes for this version: its SHA-256 isn't on Microsoft's list. Download it again from Microsoft's page.
win.evalNote: Microsoft's Windows 11 Enterprise Evaluation, downloaded from Microsoft's own server and kept only if it matches the SHA-256 Microsoft publishes. It needs no key; after {days} days it shuts down every hour.
win.legal: LordOS keeps nothing of Microsoft's: Windows comes from Microsoft's servers, and its license is between you and Microsoft. The drivers (virtio-win) come from the virtio-win project's own server.
win.how: Windows installs by itself: your account, no Microsoft account asked, privacy options off, then the drivers and guest tools. It takes 15 to 30 minutes.
win.howGuided: Windows' own installer asks everything; the drivers for its disk and network are already there.
win.keyHint: Without your key, {edition} installs with Microsoft's generic key and stays unactivated until you enter yours in Windows' Settings.
win.keyYours: Windows is activated with your key.
win.needsKey: Windows 11 Home needs your product key.
win.badKey: That isn't a product key: 25 letters and digits.
win.regional: Language {lang}, keyboard {keyboard}, time zone {tz}: this computer's.
win.r.ownIso: Your ISO, checked against Microsoft's SHA-256
un.err.winUser: 1 to 20 letters, digits, spaces, dots, - or _.
un.err.winHost: 1 to 15 letters, digits or -, not only digits.
storage.note: Copies of a machine share their storage until either of them changes, so what they share is counted once.
cfg.netNote.bridged: The machine joins the network of the card below as one more device: that network gives it an address (DHCP) and its other devices can reach it. This computer can't reach the machine over that card, and LordOS's firewall doesn't filter its traffic. Starting it needs an administrator's account.
cfg.netNote.hostonly: The machine and this computer reach each other, and nothing else: no internet, no other device. In the machine this computer is 10.0.2.2, which also reaches what this computer serves only for itself. To reach the machine from here, forward a port.
cfg.bridgeNote: Only wired cards can be bridged: a Wi-Fi network accepts one address per device.
cfg.bridgeNoCards: This computer has no wired network card, and a bridged machine needs one: over Wi-Fi it doesn't work.
cfg.portsNote: A forwarded port of this computer leads to a port of the machine: connect to 127.0.0.1 and this computer's port. Ports from 1024 up.
cfg.portsNoteHostOnly: A forwarded port of this computer leads to a port of the machine: connect to 127.0.0.1 and this computer's port. A host-only machine opens ports to this computer only.
cfg.portsLanWarn: Ports open to the network can be reached by every device on your network, and from the internet if your router forwards them. LordOS's firewall still decides: if it blocks incoming connections for Machines, the machine doesn't start.
cfg.portProblem.host: This computer's port must be {min} to 65535.
cfg.portProblem.guest: The machine's port must be 1 to 65535.
cfg.portProblem.duplicate: Another rule already uses this port of this computer.
cfg.portProblem.lanHostOnly: A host-only machine opens ports to this computer only.
cfg.secNote.networkPorts: No sockets of its own: its network goes through passt, which listens only on the forwarded ports.
cfg.secNote.networkBridged: No sockets of its own: its network is a device of the wired card (macvtap) that lord-vm opens for it, made by a closed system action. The machine is one more device on that network.
win.bridgeFailed: The bridged network couldn't be made: {why}
win.noBridgeCard: Choose its wired card in Configure, Network.
cfg.soundNote: The machine's sound plays on this computer's speakers. Changes apply at once, even while it runs.
cfg.microphoneNote: Off, the machine hears silence. On, it hears this computer's microphone while a program in it records, once you allow Machines to use the microphone (Settings → Privacy can take it back).
cfg.soundFailed: The sound settings couldn't be saved.
tb.micLive: The machine is hearing the microphone
cfg.soundOutputNote: Where the machine's sound plays. The system default follows Settings → Sound; if the chosen device isn't connected, the sound uses the default until it's back.
cfg.soundInputNote: The microphone the machine hears when the microphone is on. The system default follows Settings → Sound; if the chosen one isn't connected, the default is used.
drop.title: Drop to copy into this machine's Downloads folder
drop.none: Folders can't be copied: drop the files inside them
cfg.transferNote: A folder of this computer for moving files to and from the machine at full speed: what you drop on its window goes through it, and what the machine saves in it shows up here. In a Linux machine it's the LordOS folder in each person's home folder. The machine can write in it; nothing in it is opened or run by itself. The machine uses a little more of this computer's memory while it runs with it.
win.transferNote: In a Windows machine it's a drive once WinFsp is installed: Set Up the Transfer Folder in the machine's window (after an unattended install it's done by itself).
win.transferDrive: In the machine: a drive in This PC, usually Z:
tb.transferLinux: In the machine: the LordOS folder in your home folder
tb.transferWaiting: Not in the machine yet: it appears once the machine's agent answers
tb.transferNeedsSetup: The machine needs WinFsp for it
tb.transferReady: The transfer folder is ready in {machine}
tb.transferFailed: The transfer folder couldn't be set up in {machine}
tb.transferOff: Transfer folder off: turn it on in Configure…
drop.way.fast: Through the transfer folder, at full speed. What the machine saves in its LordOS folder shows up in Open Transfer Folder.
drop.way.agent: The transfer folder isn't ready in this machine yet: the files go through the guest agent, which is slower.
drop.way.off: The files go through the guest agent. Turn on the transfer folder in Configure for fast copies both ways.
drop.copyingFast: Copying into the machine through the transfer folder: {name}, {pct}%
drop.no.off: Start the machine to copy files into it
drop.no.paused: The machine is paused: resume it to copy files into it
drop.no.agentOff: Copying files needs the guest agent: turn it on in Configure
drop.no.agentWaiting: Copying files needs the guest agent, which isn't answering yet
drop.no.agentCant: This machine's guest agent can't write files
win.openWithUpdate: No machine can open it yet: update the LordOS tools in your Windows machine (Machines → the machine's agent button).
openWith.cant: This machine's guest tools can't open files. Install the latest LordOS tools from the agent's menu.
openWith.refused: The file couldn't be read, or it isn't in your home folder or on one of your disks.
openWith.noTools: The LordOS tools in the machine didn't connect in time. Sign in to the machine and try again.
openWith.waitTools: Waiting for the LordOS tools to open “{name}”. Sign in to the machine if it asks.
drop.refused: This can't be sent to the machine: {name}
tb.followStuck: The machine kept {w} × {h}: its display driver didn't take the window's size. Set the resolution inside the machine.
cfg.setAtCreate: Chosen when the machine was made.
apps.enter: Apps mode: each app of the machine in a window of its own
apps.needsAgent: Apps mode needs the machine's agent, connected
win.appsNeedsTools: Apps mode needs LordOS or Windows in the machine, with its LordOS tools
apps.noApps: The machine hasn't listed its apps yet
apps.gone: This window closed in the machine
apps.dropTitle: Drop to give these files to this window in the machine
apps.dropNote: They're copied into the machine first. A folder window gets them in its folder; another app gets them dropped on it or ready to paste.
apps.dropPaste: The files are in {machine}: paste them with Ctrl+V
apps.dropFolder: Copied into the folder open in {machine}
apps.dropCant: This machine's LordOS tools can't take files on a window. Update them from the agent's menu.
apps.dropMany: At most {count} files at a time: the rest were left out
apps.noWindows: No windows open in the machine
apps.closeWindow: Close this window in the machine
win.closeElevated: Can't close from here: it runs as administrator in Windows
cfg.resolutionFollowNote: The machine starts at the window's size and follows it while its system allows. The window's toolbar can still pick another size.
cfg.resolutionFixedNote: The machine starts at this size: every system takes it when it starts, also those that don't follow the window. The window's toolbar can still pick another size while it runs.
cfg.gpuNote: Intel's own driver gives the machine Direct3D 12, OpenGL and Vulkan. With a graphics card the machine can't be suspended (Suspend becomes Shut Down) or keep snapshots with its memory, and it can't have 3D graphics too.
win.gpuDriverNote: The LordOS tools install Intel's driver 27.20.100.8681 in Windows.
cfg.gpuTurnOn: Turn it on in Settings → Graphics cards.
cfg.gpuGone: No graphics card is shared with machines now: choose None, or turn one on in Settings → Graphics cards.
win.gvtOff: No graphics card is shared with machines now (Settings → Graphics cards).
win.gvtNone: Every share of the graphics card is in use by other machines.
win.gvtFailed: The graphics card couldn't be given to the machine: {why}
close.noGpuSuspend: With a graphics card it can't be suspended.
cfg.memlockNote: With a graphics card, this machine's memory is reserved for it while it runs ({n} of the {cap} all such machines may lock together).
cfg.memlockOver: With a graphics card, this machine's memory is reserved for it while it runs, and {n} is more than all such machines may lock together ({cap}): it won't start until you lower its memory or raise that limit.
win.gvtMemlock: This machine has {mem} of memory, but machines with a graphics card may lock only {cap} together (Settings → Graphics cards).
as.profileHint.games: Half of this computer's processors, a graphics card when one is set up for machines, the mouse captured.
as.customNotReady: Not checked yet: Machines settings → Systems
as.shareFolderHint: The folder this profile shares. The machine sees it as a shared folder.
as.shareFolderMissing: That folder isn't on this computer: nothing is shared.
win.sys.catalogHint: From Microsoft's servers · TPM and Secure Boot
set.title: Machines Settings
set.nav.systemsHint: The catalog and your own images
set.gen.onCloseNote: New machines take it from their profile (now {profile}); each machine's own is in its Configure → Startup.
set.gen.toolsAuto: Update the LordOS tools in machines automatically
set.gen.toolsAutoNote: The default for every machine; each one can change it in Configure.
set.logos.title: Official logos of the systems
set.logos.which: Available for: {list}. Only systems whose owners allow their logo to identify their software; the others keep LordOS's marks.
set.logos.none: No system offers its logo yet; LordOS's marks are shown.
set.logos.trademarks: Product names and logos are trademarks of their respective owners; LordOS is not affiliated with or endorsed by them. Logos are only downloaded on request, from each owner's site, and shown on this computer.
set.logos.notice: The logos are downloaded from each project's official site and stay on this computer only. The marks belong to their owners.
set.prof.text: A profile is the starting point of a new machine. You choose one when you create it, and you can change any value afterwards.
set.prof.gpuNotHere: None is set up for machines on this computer: it gets none.
set.prof.deleteDetail: Machines already made with it keep their values.
set.prof.fits: Values fit this computer on their own: never more than half of its processors nor more memory than machines may use.
set.edit.name: Name
set.edit.name.taken: You already have a profile with that name.
set.edit.author: Author
set.edit.systemNote: Only systems of the catalog, or added by you with their SHA-256. A profile never downloads anything by itself.
set.edit.gpuOnly: Only offered if this computer has one set up
set.edit.shareBad: Choose a folder in your home that isn't hidden.
set.imp.title: Import “{name}”
set.imp.intro: A profile is only values: it runs no programs. It brings the values of the machines you create with it:
set.imp.introSystem: A profile is only values: it runs no programs. It brings a new system for New machine and the values of the machines you create with it:
set.imp.httpsOnly: HTTPS only. The image isn't used until its SHA-256 matches.
set.imp.share: {path} ({how}) — you choose it when you create
set.imp.logoTheirs: A logo in a profile is its author's responsibility: LordOS doesn't host or share it.
set.imp.adj.half: “{field}: {from}” becomes {to}: never more than half of this computer.
set.imp.adj.memory: “{field}: {from}” becomes {to}: no more memory than machines may use here.
set.imp.adj.gpu: “{field}: {from}”: no graphics card is set up for machines here, none.
set.imp.adj.invalid: “{field}”: not a valid value, the default kept.
set.imp.adj.port: “{field}: {from}”: a port rule that isn't valid, left out.
set.imp.adj.system: “{field}: {from}”: a system this computer doesn't know, left out.
set.imp.ignored: “{field}”: unknown field, ignored. A profile can't run anything.
set.imp.imageRefused: An image without a SHA-256, or with an http:// address, isn't accepted.
set.imp.stays: The profile stays in your list, and you can edit or delete it.
set.imp.err.tooBig: That file is too big to be a profile.
set.imp.err.format: That profile is of a format this version doesn't know.
set.imp.err.name: That profile has no valid name.
set.sys.text: What shows in New machine. LordOS downloads each system from its official site and checks its fingerprint.
set.sys.yoursHint: Add an ISO image or an address with its SHA-256 fingerprint: you choose the name, the icon, the default profile and whether it's Linux or another system.
set.sys.chooseFile: Use a file I already downloaded…
set.sys.shaMismatch: The SHA-256 of {file} doesn't match: it isn't used.
set.sys.sigNotListed: The signed checksum file doesn't list this image's SHA-256: not used
set.sys.sigWillCheck: Signature: checked after the download with the key {fpr}
set.sys.sigWithKey: checked with its key when it downloads
set.sys.keyChanged: This system's key changed (it was {fpr}): the new one isn't used until you trust it.
set.sys.getText: LordOS downloads the image from this address into the image store every account shares (https only, a public site, at most 16 GB) and keeps it only if its SHA-256 matches. Only an administrator can download it.
set.sys.installNote: Without questions only works when the image has that installer; otherwise the install stops and says so.
set.sys.urlNote: Only https to a public site (no IP address or local network name). Copy the SHA-256 from the project's own page: the image is used only if it matches.
set.sys.sigNote: With the project's public key, LordOS checks the signature in an isolated helper and uses the image only if the signature is good and the checksum file lists its SHA-256. The first key that checks out is remembered for this system.
set.sys.logoNote: Only shown with Official logos of the systems on. This version doesn't download logos of systems you add.
set.sys.err.name: Give it a name.
set.sys.err.install: That install only exists for Linux.
set.sys.err.path: Choose an ISO in your home folder.
set.sys.err.url: That isn't a valid https address of a file.
set.sys.err.http: Only https addresses: http:// isn't accepted.
set.sys.err.key: The public key must be an armored OpenPGP block (BEGIN PGP PUBLIC KEY BLOCK), at most 32 KB.
set.sys.err.host: Only a public site's name: no IP address, localhost or local network name.
set.sys.err.sha: The SHA-256 must be 64 hexadecimal digits.
set.sys.err.signature: The signature needs its file, the checksum file (https) and a 40- or 64-digit fingerprint.
set.sys.err.logoUrl: The logo must be a PNG at an https address.
set.sys.err.logoSha: The logo's SHA-256 must be 64 hexadecimal digits.
set.net.text: How new machines reach the network. Each machine can change it in Configure → Network.
set.net.cardNote: A bridged machine joins this wired card's network as one more computer.
set.gpus.text: What Settings → Graphics cards set up for machines.
set.gpus.none: This version can't list the graphics cards.
set.gpus.one: This computer has one graphics card: it draws the desktop.
set.input.text: How a machine's window takes the keyboard and the mouse.
set.input.release: Give the keyboard back to LordOS
set.input.releaseNote: ❖Esc gives LordOS's shortcuts back while a machine has the keyboard, and takes them again.
set.input.shortcutsNote: Whether a machine's window may take ❖, ⌥Tab and the rest: asked the first time, changed in Settings → Privacy.
set.input.mouseNote: New machines take it from their profile (Keyboard and mouse): automatic, or captured on a click.
set.imp.adj.lan: Port {from} was open to your network; now only this computer.
set.imp.bridged: Bridged network: the machine joins your network as one more computer, on the card set in Machines settings → Network.
set.imp.clipBoth: The clipboard goes both ways: what you copy here can be read in the machine.
set.imp.shareWrite: The machine can change the files of the shared folder; you choose the folder when you create it.
set.edit.lanWarn: Your network: other computers on your network can reach this port.
keys.heldNote: Held until the next key you type or combination you send.
